title: BONE_INDICES values in shader incorrect when mesh has ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS set
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8] Seems to be the same in 4.3 and 4.6 ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7602) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600 CPU @ 3.50GHz (4 threads) - 15.94 GiB memory ### Issue description With some meshes the values of BONE_INDICES and BONE_WEIGHTS (spatial shader built-ins) are not what I would expect. This seems to happen with meshes with 8 bone weights instead of 4. Here's an example of where I first encountered the problem. This shader is trying to use BONE_INDICES to highlight specific bones on the mesh. The shoes mesh works as expected, highlighting faces on one specific bone, but the suit mesh has faces all over the place. And I found the shoe mesh has four bone weights per vertex while the suit has eight. The eyeballs also worked correctly and had four bone weights, while the human skin mesh had eight and showed the same problems as the suit. Here's a screenshot from the minimal reproduction, where the cube is supposed to map one face of the cube to one bone. The one on the right uses four bone weights and displays correctly, the one on the left uses 8 bone weights and is striped. Because of the stripes that appear on two faces when they should be solid on one face, I suspect the values in BONE_INDICES are getting indexed as though there are still only four per vertex, so vertex0 gets the first four values, but vertex1 gets vertex0's next four values, and vertex2 gets vertex1's first four values, and so on. Further testing indicates the extra BONE_INDICES values aren't just the extras values passed, but includes 65,535 so for some reason a max value or a negative one gets inserted in there? And the BONE_WEIGHTS end up being all 0.0 For the purposes of my shader, I would be happy with getting the first four BONE_INDICES and BONE_WEIGHTS even when the mesh has eight, but getting all these wrong values breaks the shader. ### Steps to reproduce It comes up if you try to use the BONE_INDICES in a shader with a mesh that has ARRAY_FLAG_USE_8_BONE_WEIGHTS flagged. The minimal reproduction has two generated cubes that should be identical except for the number of bone weights. You can change the values of some instanced uniforms to show how ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [bone_indices_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26146598/bone_indices_test.zip)
